intents.name: Cache Locality and Memory Hierarchy Optimization
intents.description: Improve data reuse across cache levels by blocking computation into cache-friendly tiles, reducing memory traffic and improving temporal locality.
intents.rationale: Convolution has high data reuse potential (input spatial region reused across filters, filters reused across batch/spatial). Tiling is essential on CPUs with hierarchical caches (L1/L2/L3) to minimize cache misses and maximize effective bandwidth.

transformations.name: Tiling
transformations.description: Partition loop iteration spaces into smaller blocks that fit in target cache levels.
transformations.rationale: Core technique for cache locality; enables tuning tile sizes per cache level (L1/L2) and workload shape to maximize reuse and minimize capacity misses.

transformations.name: Interchange
transformations.description: Reorder loops to change iteration order and data access patterns.
transformations.rationale: Affects which dimensions exhibit spatial/temporal locality; can expose vectorization opportunities or improve cache line utilization by changing stride patterns.

transformations.name: Packing
transformations.description: Explicitly copy and layout-transform data into contiguous scratch buffers optimized for access patterns.
transformations.rationale: Eliminates strided accesses and improves cache line utilization; critical for input/filter tensors in convolution when natural layout leads to poor spatial locality.

intents.name: SIMD Vectorization and Instruction-Level Parallelism
intents.description: Expose and exploit vector parallelism using AVX2 SIMD instructions to process multiple data elements per instruction.
intents.rationale: Target CPU has AVX2 (256-bit, 4xFP64 or 8xFP32 lanes). Vectorization is mandatory for compute efficiency; convolution's innermost reductions and spatial loops are naturally vectorizable if properly structured.

transformations.name: Vectorization
transformations.description: Transform scalar loops into vector operations mapping to SIMD instructions.
transformations.rationale: Directly exploits hardware vector units; essential for achieving peak FLOPS on modern CPUs; requires contiguous memory access and proper alignment.

transformations.name: Unrolling
transformations.description: Replicate loop bodies to expose instruction-level parallelism and reduce loop overhead.
transformations.rationale: Increases instruction window for out-of-order execution; can improve pipelining and enable better software pipelining; must balance against register pressure.

transformations.name: Peeling
transformations.description: Split off initial or final loop iterations to enable cleaner vectorization of the main loop body.
transformations.rationale: Handles boundary conditions and alignment requirements separately, allowing the bulk of iterations to be vectorized without predication or masking overhead.

intents.name: Thread-Level Parallelism and NUMA Awareness
intents.description: Distribute work across multiple CPU cores while respecting NUMA topology to exploit coarse-grain parallelism.
intents.rationale: Target system has 28 cores across 2 NUMA nodes. Convolution's batch and output channel dimensions are embarrassingly parallel; effective parallelization is critical for multi-core scaling.

transformations.name: Parallelization
transformations.description: Distribute loop iterations across threads using parallel execution primitives.
transformations.rationale: Exploits multi-core hardware; convolution naturally parallelizes over batch and filter dimensions with minimal synchronization overhead.

transformations.name: Distribution
transformations.description: Partition data and computation across NUMA nodes or hierarchical thread groups.
transformations.rationale: Improves memory bandwidth and reduces remote memory access latency on multi-socket systems; critical for large tensors spanning multiple NUMA domains.

intents.name: Computation Fusion and Operator Decomposition
intents.description: Merge or split operations to reduce memory traffic, eliminate intermediate buffers, or expose optimization opportunities.
intents.rationale: Convolution may be preceded/followed by bias addition, activation functions, or other element-wise ops. Fusing these eliminates store-load round-trips; decomposition can enable specialized optimization paths.

transformations.name: Fusion
transformations.description: Combine producer-consumer operations into a single fused kernel sharing loop nests.
transformations.rationale: Eliminates intermediate memory allocation and traffic; improves cache locality by keeping data hot; especially valuable for element-wise ops chained with convolution.

transformations.name: Decomposition
transformations.description: Break down complex operations into simpler primitives that may be easier to optimize or map to specialized instructions.
transformations.rationale: Enables targeting of specific microarchitectural features or library primitives; can expose further fusion or transformation opportunities.

intents.name: Algebraic and Algorithmic Restructuring
intents.description: Apply mathematically equivalent transformations that change computation order or representation to improve efficiency.
intents.rationale: Convolution admits multiple algorithmic formulations (direct, im2col+gemm, Winograd, FFT-based). Restructuring can better match hardware capabilities or enable library reuse.

transformations.name: Im2Col Transformation
transformations.description: Lower convolution to matrix multiplication by explicitly unrolling spatial windows into columns.
transformations.rationale: Converts convolution into GEMM, enabling reuse of highly optimized BLAS libraries; trades memory for compute efficiency and simplicity; effective for small kernels.

transformations.name: Reduction Decomposition
transformations.description: Split multi-dimensional reductions into sequences of simpler reductions or change accumulation order.
transformations.rationale: Can improve numerical stability, enable better vectorization, or expose parallelism in reduction dimensions; may reduce register pressure.

transformations.name: Loop Invariant Code Motion
transformations.description: Move computations that do not depend on inner loop variables outside those loops.
transformations.rationale: Reduces redundant computation; improves instruction scheduling; can enable better register allocation for hoisted values.

intents.name: Memory Layout and Data Format Transformation
intents.description: Change the physical layout or format of tensors in memory to match optimal access patterns for target operations.
intents.rationale: NCHW layout may not be optimal for cache or SIMD access patterns; layout transformation can eliminate strided accesses and improve vectorization-friendliness.

transformations.name: Layout Transformation
transformations.description: Convert tensor data layouts between formats such as NCHW, NHWC, blocked/tiled layouts, or custom formats.
transformations.rationale: Optimizes spatial locality and access stride for target hardware; blocked layouts can improve cache efficiency; certain formats enable better vectorization.

transformations.name: Padding and Alignment
transformations.description: Insert padding to align data structures to cache line or vector register boundaries.
transformations.rationale: Eliminates unaligned memory accesses and cache line splits; ensures vector loads/stores are efficient; can prevent false sharing in parallel code.

intents.name: Bufferization and Intermediate Materialization Control
intents.description: Control where and how intermediate results are materialized, balancing memory footprint against recomputation.
intents.rationale: Convolution generates large intermediate activations; deciding what to buffer versus recompute affects memory bandwidth and cache pressure; critical in memory-constrained scenarios.

transformations.name: Bufferization Strategy
transformations.description: Specify policies for when to allocate buffers for intermediate tensor values versus keeping them in registers or recomputing.
transformations.rationale: Manages register pressure and memory traffic trade-offs; in-place updates can reduce allocation overhead; important for controlling peak memory usage.

transformations.name: Scratch Allocation Optimization
transformations.description: Optimize allocation and reuse of temporary buffers for packed data or intermediate tiles.
transformations.rationale: Reduces dynamic allocation overhead; improves cache residency of scratch data; enables stack allocation for small tiles; can prevent heap fragmentation.

intents.name: Loop Transformation for Instruction Scheduling
intents.description: Restructure loops to improve instruction pipelining, hide latencies, and maximize instruction throughput.
intents.rationale: Modern CPUs rely on deep pipelines and out-of-order execution; loop transformations can increase independent instruction streams and improve instruction-level parallelism beyond vectorization.

transformations.name: Loop Jamming
transformations.description: Merge adjacent loops into a single loop body to increase instruction count per iteration and reduce loop overhead.
transformations.rationale: Expands loop bodies, giving schedulers more instructions to reorder; can hide latencies; reduces branch misprediction penalties by decreasing loop count.

transformations.name: Loop Skewing
transformations.description: Transform loop bounds to change dependence patterns and enable better parallelization or pipelining.
transformations.rationale: Breaks certain loop-carried dependencies or enables wavefront parallelism; can improve cache reuse in specific access patterns.

transformations.name: Strip Mining
transformations.description: Split a loop into an outer loop over strips and an inner loop over elements within each strip.
transformations.rationale: Provides explicit control over iteration chunk sizes; useful for register blocking or matching instruction queue depth; precursor to tiling.

intents.name: Specialization and Predication Elimination
intents.description: Generate specialized code paths for common cases or eliminate conditional overhead within hot loops.
intents.rationale: Generic convolution code contains conditionals for boundary handling, padding, and stride logic; specialization can eliminate branches in inner loops, improving pipelining and reducing mispredictions.

transformations.name: Loop Splitting
transformations.description: Separate loop iterations into multiple loops based on conditions, creating specialized paths for boundary versus interior cases.
transformations.rationale: Eliminates conditionals from inner loops; enables aggressive optimization of the common interior case; simplifies dependence analysis.

transformations.name: Constant Propagation and Folding
transformations.description: Evaluate expressions involving compile-time constants to simplify control flow and reduce runtime computation.
transformations.rationale: Exposes further optimization opportunities; can turn dynamic conditionals into static decisions; simplifies code generation.

transformations.name: Predicate Elimination
transformations.description: Remove or minimize predicated execution or masked operations within vectorized loops.
transformations.rationale: Predication introduces overhead on CPUs without full mask support; eliminating masks via loop splitting or peeling improves vector instruction efficiency.

intents.name: Canonicalization and IR Simplification
intents.description: Apply standard compiler simplifications to normalize IR, expose optimization opportunities, and enable pattern matching.
intents.rationale: Transformations introduce complexity and redundancy; canonicalization ensures IR remains analyzable and optimization-friendly; critical for enabling downstream passes.

transformations.name: Canonicalization
transformations.description: Apply standard simplification patterns such as dead code elimination, common subexpression elimination, and algebraic identities.
transformations.rationale: Cleans up IR after transformations; exposes further opportunities; ensures consistent IR form for pattern matching in subsequent passes.

transformations.name: Affine Simplification
transformations.description: Simplify affine expressions, bounds, and maps to canonical forms to improve analysis precision.
transformations.rationale: Enables more accurate dependence analysis and legality checking; simplifies bounds for polyhedral optimizations; reduces representation overhead.

transformations.name: Loop Normalization
transformations.description: Standardize loop bounds to start at zero and increment by one, simplifying further transformations.
transformations.rationale: Normalizes loop analysis; makes bounds checking and transformation application more uniform; simplifies code generation.
